title: Ref
description: An exact reference to an input (docs/design/m0/10 "Refs and fingerprints"). Canonical form: lineage, restrictions and each restriction's allowed_destinations are sets, written sorted (strings by Unicode code point; restrictions by project, policy_digest, floor, routing, then allowed_destinations compared element by element, a shorter prefix first), without duplicates, and an empty set is [] (never null or absent). identity_digest is "sha256:" followed by the lowercase hex SHA-256 of the RFC 8785 (JCS) encoding of the canonical ref without identity_digest, so a change of revision, scope, lineage or restrictions changes the identity even when the bytes are identical. Content deduplication never merges restrictions.

id.description: A digest, a git id and path, or a controller id, by type.

revision.description: E.g. an adopted contract revision; null when the type has none.

framework.description: Framework scope: about auto-dev-cycle itself, never a project's code or domain.

lineage.description: The ids of the refs this one was derived from, recorded by the controller.

restrictions.description: Source restrictions inherited through lineage (KA1): every distinct snapshot of a contributing project's data policy is kept, several per project when the ref was derived from inputs under different policy revisions, wherever the ref goes. All apply together: a delivery must satisfy each one. They record lineage; they never replace the live checks at each delivery (initial, lookup, fallback) of the receiving project's policy, revocation and export approval.

Restriction.description: The data policy of a contributing project when the ref was derived from it: a receiving project and destination must satisfy every restriction at each delivery.

policy_digest.description: Of the project's adopted data policy.

allowed_destinations.description: Resolved destinations, recorded when the restriction is: here an empty set means no destination may receive the ref (never 'derived from the usage profile').
